descriptionChirho: A living tree or a large wooden structure, especially (a) the cross on which Jesus was crucified, referred to euphemistically as 'the tree' following Deut 21:22-23, and (b) the eschatological tree of life in Revelation. For the cross: Acts 5:30, 10:39, 13:29 'hanging him on a xulon', Gal 3:13 'cursed is everyone hanged on a xulon', 1 Pet 2:24 'bore our sins in his body on the xulon.' These are rendered arb 'khashaba' (wooden beam), heb 'etz' (tree/wood), spa 'madero' (timber beam), hin 'kath' (wooden frame). For the tree of life: Rev 2:7, 22:2, 14, 19, rendered arb 'shajara' (living tree), spa 'arbol' (tree), hin 'vrksh' (tree), kor 'namu' (tree). The Arabic shift from 'khashaba' (hewn beam) to 'shajara' (living tree) marks a semantic sub-distinction between cross-timber and living tree, but the underlying Greek xulon spans both as a single polysemous range centered on 'large piece of wood / tree.'

A short thick stick used as a weapon; a club or cudgel carried for striking. Used exclusively in the arrest scenes of the Synoptic passion narratives: Matt 26:47, 55 ('you came out with swords and xuloi to arrest me'), Mark 14:43, 48 (same scene), Luke 22:52 ('you came out as against a robber with swords and xuloi'). Cross-linguistically rendered with weapon-specific vocabulary distinct from all other senses: arb 'isiyin' (sticks/rods), deu 'Holz' (general), heb 'maklot' (sticks/rods, from makel = staff), hin 'lathiyon' (bamboo staves/lathis, the traditional South Asian police baton), kor 'mongdungidl' (cudgels), spa 'palos' (sticks/clubs). The Hindi 'lathi' rendering is particularly telling as it designates a specific weapon-stick rather than generic wood.

Wood as a raw material or substance, not a living tree or shaped weapon. In Luke 23:31 Jesus says 'if they do these things in the green xulon, what will happen in the dry?' (proverbial: green vs. dry wood), rendered hin 'lakdi' (firewood/lumber), spa 'leno' (log). In 1 Cor 3:12 Paul lists building materials including 'xula' (wood pieces) alongside gold, silver, and precious stones, rendered heb 'etzim' (wood pieces), hin 'lakdi' (wood), spa 'maderas' (timbers). In Rev 18:12 Babylon's luxury cargo includes 'xulon thuinon' (citrus wood) and other precious wood, rendered arb 'khashab' (timber), hin 'lakdi' (wood), spa 'madera' (wood). The consistent hin 'lakdi' (raw timber/lumber) and spa 'madera/maderas' (wood material) distinguish this from tree (arbol/vrksh) and club (palos/lathiyon).

A wooden instrument of punishment and restraint in which a prisoner's feet (and sometimes hands) are locked between two planks. Used once in Acts 16:24 where the Philippian jailer 'fastened their feet in the xulon' (stocks) after Paul and Silas were imprisoned. Cross-linguistically rendered with specialized penal vocabulary wholly distinct from all other senses of xulon: arb 'miqtara' (pillory/stocks, a specific imprisonment device), deu 'Holz' (general), heb 'sad' (stocks, the specific OT term for this instrument, cf. Jer 20:2-3, 29:26), hin 'kath' (wooden frame/stocks), kor 'chakkob' (stocks/shackles), spa 'cepo' (stocks/pillory). The Hebrew 'sad' is a technical term for foot-stocks found in prophetic literature, confirming this as a distinct lexicalized sense of xulon.
